The repaired model is in `work/edited`: on practice it scores worst-group 91.2% (was 72.9%) and weighted mean 95.4% (was 97.7%), and the held-out estimates are essentially the same. All 50 forward passes are used.

## What I changed (7 tensors)

1. **Layer4's entrance** — `layer4.0.conv1.weight` and `layer4.0.downsample.0.weight`, with `layer4.0.bn1.running_mean` and `layer4.0.downsample.1.running_mean`. Both 1×1 convolutions that read layer3's output are made blind to two background directions of that output, which are replaced by their group-balanced mean values via the running means:
   - `u3`: the water-minus-land mean difference, bird class held fixed.
   - `q3`: the top eigenvector of (water-image covariance − land-image covariance), orthogonal to `u3`.
2. **The last block's reader** — `layer4.2.conv1.weight` with `layer4.2.bn1.running_mean`. It is made blind to the background mean-difference direction of its input, measured on the model after edit 1.
3. **`fc.bias`** — the waterbird-minus-landbird bias is raised by log(0.7679/0.2321) = 1.196, the class prior implied by the training proportions in the task. `fc.weight` is untouched.

Nothing was fitted to labels: the directions are group mean differences and one covariance eigenvector, and the bias shift comes from the stated training proportions.

## What goes wrong in the network

- **The margin is nearly additive in bird and background.** Group mean margins are −13.7 / −4.9 / +3.0 / +10.3, i.e. a bird effect of 16.0 and a background effect of 8.1, with within-group SD of about 5.
- **Background is linearly coded from layer3 on; bird only inside layer4.** Held-out background separation is about 2.3 SD at layer3 and 2.6–2.9 through layer4. The two directions are orthogonal at layer3 (cos 0.04) and aligned after the last block (0.57).
- **Layer4 turns the background code into class evidence, serially.** Blinding one reader at a time reduces the 8.08 step to 2.80 (layer4.0's two readers), 5.42 (`layer4.1.conv1`), 3.25 (`layer4.2.conv1`) and 0 (fc). These reductions add to more than the total because each block re-reads the same code off the skip path.
- **The response to "wateriness" saturates.** Blinding only `u3` equalises group means but over-corrects very watery scenes (landbird margin −16 there versus −5 on ambiguous scenes). Adding `q3` flattens this and improved waterbird/water accuracy from 88.7% to 93.2%.

## Evidence for the edits

- **Dose-response.** Edit 1 at strengths 0 / 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 gives a background step of 8.08 / 5.71 / 2.80 / −0.34, with the bird effect at 16.0 / 15.8 / 15.7 / 15.5. The later reader edits at 0 / 0.5 / 1 take the remaining step 2.80 → 1.70 → 0.44.
- **Specificity.** Blinding the same readers to non-background directions they read at least as strongly changes nothing (step 7.88; later stages 2.81 versus 2.80).
- **The running-mean edits are needed.** Without them, waterbird/land drops to 67.7%. The neutral point acts only on the class offset, and the balanced mean keeps the model's own offset.
- **Controlled composites.** Twelve bird patches were pasted on eleven bird-free backgrounds. The same patch scores +5.6 higher on water surrounds in the original and −0.4 ± 0.4 in the final model. Bird-free land versus water scenes go from −6.9 / +5.2 to −0.5 / +0.2, with class separation preserved (15.5 → 15.2).
- **Out-of-sample.** The whole chain was rebuilt from one half of the practice images and scored on the other half, both ways. Only 7 of 1,199 predictions differ from the in-sample version.

| Final model | LL | LW | WL | WW | Worst | Weighted mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Original | 99.4 | 82.6 | 72.9 | 96.2 | 72.9 | 97.7 |
| Practice, in-sample | 96.4 | 91.2 | 92.5 | 93.2 | 91.2 | 95.4 |
| Practice, held-out halves | 96.8 | 90.6 | 92.5 | 93.2 | 90.6 | 95.7 |
| Mirrored practice images | 95.9 | 92.7 | 92.5 | 94.0 | 92.5 | 95.3 |

Paired against the original on practice: waterbird/land gains 26 and loses 0; landbird/water gains 43 and loses 3; landbird/land loses 14; waterbird/water loses 4.

## Things I got wrong or dropped

- **"The last layer is too late" was wrong.** Projecting the background direction out of fc alone costs 44% of the bird effect but shrinks the noise equally, giving the same separability and held-out [98.7, 92.7, 90.2, 91.0] with no bias shift. I kept the upstream repair because it preserves the evidence scale and class offset, so the prior correction applies unambiguously; with fc-only the right shift is unclear.
- **A third edit on `layer4.1.conv1` was removed.** With the last block's reader blinded it added nothing measurable (held-out [96.8, 90.8, 92.5, 93.2] with it, [96.8, 90.6, 92.5, 93.2] without).
- **Other variants gave no gain:** an fc projection of the residual direction, a 12-dimensional subspace at stage 1, and partner directions at later stages. Every route lands at a bird effect of about 3.3 SD, which looks like the ceiling of the network's bird features.
- **One mechanism is unresolved.** After edit 1 alone, natural images keep a 2.8-unit step that the composites barely show. My "near the bird" explanation failed its test and an occluder test was inconclusive.

## What to expect on the test set

I expect roughly 96–97 / 91 / 92–93 / 93, i.e. worst group about 91% and mean about 95.5%. The standard errors are about 1.3 points for landbird/water, 2.3 for each waterbird group and 0.8 for the mean. A rough estimate of the chance of meeting both targets is 0.9; it is flat around the prior shift I used, so I did not tune it.

Two things cap the remaining errors. About a third of the landbird/water errors I viewed (10 of 32) have real water birds or animals in the background photo; with the pasted landbird removed, those backgrounds still score "waterbird". And some "waterbird"-labelled species are actually land species (wood-pewee, towhee), which the model calls landbirds regardless of background.

Copies of the final tensors are in `work/final_v2/`, and `work/notes.md` has the full log.
